pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
Our Vision
We strive to deliver the best early years education and support to children and their families. Our core aim is to develop and prepare our children, some of whom have additional barriers to learning, by equipping them and their families with the skills, knowledge and attitude to succeed in their next steps, be confident in themselves and hold high aspirations for their futures. We believe all children should have access to high quality personalised learning and support, no matter what their ability or needs.
​Our Golden Values
We are curious, confident and independent learners. We embrace new experiences, persevere when things feel challenging and take pride in our achievements.​
Be Ready
Be Kind
Be Safe

Early Years Pupil Premium
To determine whether or not children are eligible for this funding we ask all families to complete an EYPP declaration form when your child starts Nursery.
To find out how we are using this, please read the full EYPP report.

Parenting Courses
This nurturing group is run by our qualified Family Support Worker and encourages bonding with your baby and increases parents' confidence in handling their baby. This group helps to reduce isolation for new mums and provides a welcoming and safe space to meet new people. This group is held in our Badgers building on Mondays from 1 - 2.30pm. The five week course must be booked in advance.
Our qualified and experienced team deliver this parenting course based on funding and demand from our families. In the course, you will be given some ideas of how to understand your children’s behaviour and some strategies to put in place to help support children. Look at the value of consistent parenting, having fun and giving praise. Whilst still nurturing yourself to be able to share empathy, understanding and enjoy being a parent. This course must be booked in advance and is run on either a 4 week or 10 week basis. Please email bookings@bushyleaze.hants.sch.uk for more information.
This is group aimed at young parents suitable for those with children from birth up to 5 years old. The group aims to support parents and carers to enhance their children's learning and development and improve their life chances by making the most of everyday learning opportunities. Through this, babies and children become confident communicators and active learners. This is about valuing and building on what parents already do - sharing ideas from parents, practitioners, and also understanding why they help children's later development. This group is run on Tuesdays from 1 - 2.30pm.
Join our new cooking courses and learn about cooking delicious meals for the family while saving money. The courses will build your confidence in preparing cost effective and nutritionally balanced meals, increase your knowledge and awareness of the nutritional needs of your family in a social environment with other parents. Our weaning sessions are great to learn helpful tips about preparing and serving food for your babies. These sessions are advertised accordingly and must be booked in advance.

Starting Nursery
Before your child starts with us we will be happy to show you around and talk about your child’s needs and what we can offer. We will visit you at home in order to get to know your child and will spend as much time as we can learning about them, completing an ‘All About Me’ booklet with you.
We want to work in partnership with you to ensure that your child settles quickly into nursery. We want you to feel welcome too so please tell us at any time if you have any concerns, we will always listen and help if we can. We want every child to feel happy and confident with us, some children take longer to settle than others and we understand if you need to stay with your child for a little while. This is a very important step for your child and if it is handled sensitively it will give him/her greater confidence in other new situations.
Every child will have a key person and a key buddy who will work closely with you so that learning is supported and information is shared. We promote education as a partnership with parents.

Governors
We have a flat governing body model in which all governors share equal responsibility for leadership, oversight, and strategic direction for the centre.
Governors are elected to serve for 4 years and meet to discuss issues relevant to the management of the Nursery. To find out more click on this link.

Our Curriculum
At Bushy Leaze, we believe every child is unique, capable, and full of potential. Our children are at the heart of our curriculum, with child-led play, nurturing relationships, and meaningful experiences helping our children grow in confidence, develop independence, strengthen their communication skills, and become happy, resilient learners with a lifelong love of learning.
Our Golden Threads that run through our curriculum are:
Communication and language
Personal, social and emotional skills
These are prioritised across our provision and underpin all learning.
Looking After Ourselves
Lenny Lion represents 'Be Ready' and encourages us to be active and 'Keep Busy'. This helps the children to be ready to learn about looking after themselves and make healthy, positive choices.
Caring for our World
Casper Cat represents 'Be Kind' and encourages us to connect and 'Come Together'. This helps the children to be kind and care for themselves, one another, and the natural world.
Being Part of our Community
Pip Penguin represents 'Be Safe' and he likes to take notice and 'Keep Discovering'. This helps the children to become ready and confident learners both at Bushy Leaze and in the wider community.

pageCache.pageTitle: How to... Have Healthier Screen Time | Bushy Leaze Childr 1
pageCache.text:
Top Tips for Healthier Screen Time
Smartphones can be great for learning, but they shouldn't replace time with adults. Passive screen time or caregivers being distracted by their phone, means less time for vital back and forth interactions. These are so important for children's brain development and social skills. This video "How every child can thrive by five" explains the vital role caregivers play. Who knew that a game of peek-a-boo could change the world!
Screens should not be used as a distraction. Purposeful screen time with an adult can be both educational and fun. However, young children learn best through exploring their surroundings and having real-life experiences. Activities like playing outside, reading books together, and hands-on learning are invaluable for their development.
Under 2s: Avoid independent screen time. Use screens only for interactive, shared, or social bonding activities.
Aged 2-5: Limit to 1 hour daily.​​

pageCache.pageTitle: How to... Prevent Choking Hazards | Bushy Leaze Childr 1
pageCache.text:
Avoid Choking Hazards
Young children have narrow airways and are still learning to chew, breathe and swallow in the right order - add talking or moving around and it gets really complicated!
STAY – Stay with children when they’re eating – it’s the biggest thing you can do for them
STILL – Get children to sit still – it can be a battle but it’s much safer
Small round food, such as grapes and cherry tomatoes should be cut lengthways and into quarters.
Large fruit and vegetables such as melon or apple and carrot should be cut into longer thinner slices instead of small chunks.
If inhaled, a balloon or bits of a broken balloon can seal a child’s airway. They can be very hard to remove.
So, avoid giving young children balloons to blow up and clear away any broken bits straight away.
Remember - Anything smaller than a 2 pence piece can choke a young child.
Think carefully about the toys and food you give your child.

pageCache.pageTitle: How to... Stop Passive Smoking and Vapes | Bushy Leaze Childr 1
pageCache.text:
Passive Smoking
Second hand smoke is a lethal cocktail of more than 4,000 irritants, toxins and cancer-causing substances.
Most second hand smoke is invisible and odourless, so no matter how careful you think you're being, people around you still breathe in the harmful poisons.
Passive smoking is especially harmful for children as they have less well-developed airways, lungs and immune systems.
If you would like some help to quit smoking, then click on the link.
Vaping
21% of 11-17 year olds have tried vaping? (ASH 2023) And this is on the rise.
Side effects can include headaches, coughing, insomnia and exposure to nicotine which is highly addictive.
Disposable vapes also generate lots of single use plastic, electrical waste and litter.
Although vaping is safer than smoking, vapes should only be used by people who currently smoke.
For more information and help to quit smoking or vaping visit smokefreehampshire

We are proud of our nursery and what each and every one of our children achieve. We would like to share with you how we work and what you can expect when your child joins us.

Our Classes
The children are welcomed into three zones; The Nest, The Burrow and The Den. Our children are able to move between these zones, so they can learn and play where it is best for them. Each area of the nursery provides all children with the environment, resources, staff and activities appropriate to their level of development and need. You can be confident that all of our staff:
are trained and experienced in working with young children
will give your child lots of praise and attention
will keep your child safe, happy and interested
will help your child communicate and help them make choices
will teach them skills
will encourage their curiosity, active learning and sense of awe and wonder

Parenting Support
Our bookable community outreach groups offer support to families with babies and toddlers in and around Alton. These groups support families dealing with isolation, anxiety, financial challenges and family crisis, offering a safe place to visit and opportunities to develop vital friendship networks. We can signpost to our own specialist support and other agencies depending on individual needs.
Our specialist targeted programmes offer in excess of 200 referred places per year, supporting families with specific issues such as
mental health challenges
getting to know your baby through baby massage
support for families who may have concerns about speech, language and communication
children with special educational needs and disabilities
developing parenting skills
parents seeking to go back into employment
In addition, many families with children under 5 receive dedicated 1:1 support from Bushy Leaze expert Family Support Team, ranging from half-an-hour advice to receiving ongoing weekly contact to help them through their times of need.

What Matters - Back to Basics
Looking after your family’s wellbeing is really important, and every family needs a bit of support from time to time as life changes or new challenges come up.
As a parent or carer, you can help your child’s wellbeing and your own by taking small, simple steps. Focusing on What Matters can help you feel more in control and make positive changes using the 5 ways to wellbeing.
Start by choosing just one area to think about. Look at your home life and consider what small, manageable changes you and your family could try together.​
Click on the link, check our What Matters noticeboard, or speak to someone in the nursery if you’d like support or ideas. Don't forget to check Tapestry and our weekly newsletter too!
